findings.title: Raw recovery codes are sent to and expected to be stored by user storage
findings.body: The local path stores RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, whose credential data contains hashed recovery codes, but the federated path serializes the raw generatedCodes and passes them as the UserCredentialModel challenge response. A user-storage provider that persists this value as received, as the new test provider does, therefore stores all unused recovery codes in recoverable plaintext. Disclosure of the external store would reveal valid second-factor bypass codes, defeating the hashing used for local credentials; the federated input should carry hashed code data or otherwise not require plaintext persistence.

findings.title: Successful federated recovery-code use is never consumed
findings.body: After credentialManager().isValid succeeds, this code only removes the credential when allCodesUsed() is already true; it never records consumption of the just-used code in federated storage (for example via an updateCredential call). For a federated credential, allCodesUsed() is computed from data returned by the storage provider, and a provider whose isValid only validates, like the added BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, leaves every code unused. The same recovery code can therefore be replayed indefinitely and the all-used removal/required-action branch is never reached, violating the single-use property of recovery codes.

findings.title: Federated creation discards recovery credential label and generation time
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential receives a fully populated RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel containing the user label and generated-at timestamp, but for the user-storage path it builds UserCredentialModel("", type, rawCodesJson) and discards everything except the type and codes. Providers consequently cannot persist the label or original creation date; later reads must synthesize a date and lose the label, so account/admin credential metadata for federated recovery codes differs from locally stored credentials created from the same required action.

findings.title: Federated getCredentials returns a recovery credential with a different ID from the stored one
findings.body: updateCredential assigns recoveryCodesModel an ID via KeycloakModelUtils.generateId(), but getCredentials builds a fresh RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues without copying myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() (unlike the OTP branch, which returns the stored model). Callers such as the authenticator's all-codes-used cleanup use credentialModel.getId() to remove the credential, so that ID will not match the stored federated credential and removal/identification cannot work reliably; the test double masks real ID-based lifecycle behavior.
